Bingham County, Idaho

Bingham County is a county located in the southeast region of Idaho, United States. It was established in 1885 and is named after Henry Harriman Bingham, who was a prominent figure in the area's early history. With a population of just over 45,000 people, Bingham County is a small but thriving community that offers a high quality of life and a variety of opportunities to its residents.

Demographics of Bingham County

Bingham County has a population of 45,171 people, with a growth rate of 2.2% over the past decade. The county is ethnically and racially diverse, with a mix of white, Hispanic, Native American, and African American residents.

Economy of Bingham County

The economy of Bingham County is primarily driven by agriculture, manufacturing, and retail trade. Major industries in the county include food processing, renewable energy, and advanced manufacturing. The unemployment rate in Bingham County is low, at just 4.4%.

Education in Bingham County

Bingham County is home to a number of excellent schools and higher education institutions. The county is served by the Blackfoot School District, which includes several elementary, middle, and high schools. Higher education options in the county include Idaho State University and the College of Eastern Idaho.

Healthcare is readily available in Bingham County, with several hospitals and clinics located throughout the area. Residents have access to a wide range of health services, including preventive care, medical and surgical treatments, and rehabilitation services.

Bingham County is well connected by roadways and highways, with major roads like I-15 and US-26 running through the area. Public transportation options are limited, but the county does have a bus system that provides regular service to major destinations.

Bingham County is a culturally rich area, with a variety of arts and entertainment options available. The county is also home to several parks and outdoor recreation areas, including the Snake River and the Blackfoot Reservoir. There are also several golf courses, hiking trails, and fishing spots in the area.

The real estate market in Bingham County is thriving, with a variety of homes available to suit any budget and lifestyle. The average home price in the county is around $200,000, and there are many affordable options available, as well as more luxurious properties.

Bingham County is a safe place to live, with low crime rates and a strong law enforcement presence. The county is served by the Bingham County Sheriff's Office, which is dedicated to ensuring the safety and well-being of residents.

Bingham County is governed by a board of county commissioners, who are elected by the residents of the county. The county is predominantly Republican, with a strong conservative base.

Bingham County has a temperate climate, with average temperatures ranging from the high 30s to the low 90s throughout the year. The county receives moderate precipitation, with the majority of the rain falling during the spring and summer months. Severe weather events, such as thunderstorms and tornadoes, are relatively rare in the area.
